Debug travis/Fix bug

The tests were failing on Travis (and only travis). The reason was that
I was using a comparison operator (<) for cci::List iterators. But the
comparison operator makes only sense for random access operators. In
particular, I can't assume that the nodes in a list are located in a
contiguous memory.

Add solution to Q7, Chapter 2
Add solution to Q5, Chapter2, and fix GCC build

Refactor cci:List

The refactoring includes:
  * add a list sentinel to ease dealing with list's beginning and end
  and to mimic the implementation in std::list in libstdc++
  * make the API more like std::list (got rid of some of the old API
  methods)
  * more unit tests for cci::List (also moved them to a seperate file)
  * remove partition2 (well, partition does the same thing, but better)
  * added iterators for const objects

Add solution to Q5, Chapter 2

This is only a solution for cases where numbers are stored in reverse
order. If numbers are stored in "natural" order, then dealing with
"carry" values requires a doubly-linked list.

Do small refactoring for Q4, Chapter 2

I was experimenting a bit, but ended up just tidying up a tiny bit.

Revert changes in CMake regarding

Using "-Wno-gnu-zero-variadic-macro-arguments" only worked for clang.
GCC doesn't recognise that option, so the build would still fail. I
removed "-Wpedantic" instead. The corresponding issue is reported here:
  https://github.com/google/googletest/issues/1419

Get rid of all warnings and enable Werror

This also required removing an unused variable which would make Werror
unhappy.

Update solution to Q4, Chapter 2 for std::list

The previous solution was a hack - it took as input any list, but then
internally worked with cci::List and also always returned cci::List.
This patch adds a seperate implementation for std::list based on
std::partition.

Fix GCC build

Turns out that I need a move-constructor, not a copy-constructor for
cci::list. For whatever reason clang was happy with that, but GCC caught
that.

Also applied clang-format.

Add solution to Q4, Chapter 2

Also includes minor refactoring to conform to Google's coding style

Add a solution to Q3, Chapter 2 using iterators

This patch adds cci::List::erase, that mimics std::list::erase. This
basically implements a solution to Q3, Chapter 2. Unit tests were added
accordingly.

Add solution to Q3, chapter 2, and iterators to cci::List

The main puprose of this patch was to add solution to Q3. But I also
wanted to write more generic code indepenedent of the underlying
implementation of the linked list. As such, this patch also adds
ForwardIterator to cci::List.

[Travis] Add clang to the build system

Since the default version of clang available in Travis doesn't support
C++17, a newer version has to be installed. The build the requires env
variables to be set accordingly (so that the latest version of clang is
used). Since similar steps are required for GCC, this patch creates a
Travis matrix to make this possible/easy.

Fix Travis CI build

This project uses C++17 features and the default set-up on Travis
doesn't provide a compatible compiler. This patch will make sure that
the required packages are installed. However, only GCC for now (so CMake
had to be updated too).
Update README.md and add .travis.yml

Fix memory leak in tests-ch1.cpp

Since std::string.length() doesn't include the terminating null
character, one must add 1 extra character when allocating space for a
C-string based on an instance of std::string. That wasn't the case in
one of tests. Although the tests worked just fine, that was UB.
